codex2 posted required STORY1843 REST/MCP/core writer + remove/reset/poolreuse/clone + ACTUAL held-lock inventory, source main3cbb90b0c94e0e748bbfc4eb1f75d7f9c2125c68. Canonical inventory plus exact-symbol clarification posted; corrected local /tmp/codex2-story1843-writer-retirement-lock-inventory.txt.
Key verified facts: REST assignment explicitly drops Tokio store guard and completes queue call before core write; core::write_local_message covers REST/direct/system writers but has NO lifecycle fence. Canonical digest has SEPARATE private writer inside re-entrant Store lock; push/pull capture local before Store but publish inside. Pool acquire/return/destroy reset/remove under pool.lock; generic teardown removes BEFORE taking pool lock for deregistration. Dispatch finalize writes notice under tick.lock; seat takeover explicitly drops SeatGuard before notice. Native grant and current-session read checks acquire no update/allocation flock; occupancy authorize can retain SeatGuard in SeatPermit. MCP handle_request heartbeat may allocate namespace, so must not become receipt-lock revalidation callback.
Concrete C gaps: session_end/force_cleanup_lease lose lease/recovery state before removal refusal; raw gc/dismiss/compete/startup rollback/dispatch cleanup/reuse and seat_clone remove_dir_all bypass common remover. Integrator direct reset bypasses pool. Ignored mail can survive poolreset and leak to next occupant. Opaque hooks under pool.lock mean no honest globally-acyclic graph claim. Lowest seams/held-permit variants, explicit outerPool→Lifecycle and pre-Store canonical admission, Lifecycle→Receipt, no Receipt→Seat/Namespace/Store, protected read-only version recheck, and exact required restructuring choices are recorded. No current runtime-deadlock exploit invented: Receipt/Lifecycle are proposed new locks, not existing ones.
B binding incorporated: timestamp-only legacy watermark is UnknownLegacy, NEW explicit selected delivery ACK remains possible; per-response postflush semantics/observable failures; no new floor/authority bypass. C3 must fence/quiesce actual old REST/MCP/core/in-flight/hook mutators, not trust version or copy/openFD. Verified-clone retention binding remains an explicit choice; unknown clone refuses, no borrowed main anchor. No source/Cargo/claims/grants/ACK/install/migration/live tests; A2345/46/fullC-D-E not waived. ReadyBUG2222 or routed2919newhead remains review priority; this bounded inventory is complete as an entry/callchain assessment with concrete implementation gaps, not implementation approval.
